description.value: Bates Beach Farm is a small family-run farm market in the Comox Valley, situated beside Seal Bay Regional Park on Vancouver Island's east coast. It exploits an ocean-influenced microclimate to grow standout berries, tomatoes, garlic, and peppers, with a declared focus on Mediterranean-style produce. In addition to fresh seasonal fruit and vegetables, the market carries house-made frozen soups and fresh salsas, and also hosts a booth at the Comox Valley Farmers Market.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms an operational farm market at 5700 Bates Road, Courtenay, selling home-grown produce and house-made soups and salsas. Phone (250-897-6202) and address both match OSM. No mention of bike parking, water access, washrooms, or any cycling-specific amenities anywhere on the site or in OSM tags, so those are null. The farm's location beside Seal Bay Regional Park on a cycling-accessible road makes it a plausible cyclist stop, but amenity evidence is thin.
concerns: Contact page still references COVID-19 mask guidelines, suggesting the page has not been updated in some time; core business details appear current.
Two different email addresses appear on the site (batesbeachmike@gmail.com on the home page; mike@oceansideindustrial.ca on the contact page) — primary contact email is ambiguous.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Active farm market selling fresh local produce beside Seal Bay Regional Park; a practical resupply stop for cyclists touring the Comox Valley, even though cycling-specific amenities are unconfirmed.
